newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Zinc chief urges caution as market improves.
newsitem.headline: Zinc chief urges caution as market improves.

text.p: The zinc industry, emerging from five years of crisis, must avoid rushing headlong into a major expansion of capacity, the head of one of the world's leading producers, Union Miniere, said on Monday.
"One major threat to the industry will come from the industry itself," Karel Vinck, chief executive officer of Belgian non-ferrous metals group Union Miniere, told a zinc conference.
He said Western smelter projects for an extra 1.4 million tonnes a year were under study, of which 30 percent were in North America and 20 percent in Australia.
Higher prices and lower stocks could also encourage former communist countries to develop new projects and a considerable amount of idle world capacity could be brought back on stream.
If the zinc industry wasn't careful it could re-create the conditions that led to the start of the crisis in the early 1990s, he warned.
Vinck cautiously expected the average world zinc price to be between $1,200 and $1,250 per tonne in 1997.
"It could be considered a conservative view, but it's on the basis of industrial plans," he told the conference.
Industry analysts have been more bullish, forecasting zinc prices climbing above $1,300 a tonne in 1997. Vinck's forecast was slightly more optimistic than one he made last month of $1,200 per tonne.
During the recent crisis zinc prices fell to $880 a tonne, from a peak of $1,400 in 1992 before climbing again.
Although stocks on the London Metal Exchange have fallen after soaring to 1.24 million tonnes, they are still twice the level of five years ago.
Vinck said that zinc mining and smelting companies must adopt a global strategy in order to meet future challenges.
"We have to prepare our companies to operate more and more on a world-wide scale," he told the conference organised by Metal Bulletin.

Despite substantial restructuring in recent years, there were still a large number of players, he said, adding that further rationalisation was likely in order for companies to be competitive on world markets.

The industry must also adopt a common approach to dealing with growing environmental constraints, especially in the European Union, concerning iron waste residues from smelters and pollution damage, he said, adding, zinc recycling was also of growing importance.
Union Miniere has two major zinc refineries at Balen, northern Belgium, and at Auby, northern France, with combined capacity of over 450,000 tonnes per year.
